channel.description: WSJ World News RSS, without Opinions

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts of November 2026: Up to 5.00%
item.description: Beat average interest rates with one of these top high-yield savings accounts.

item.title: Iran Escalates Low-Level Conflict With a Shot at Bahrain
item.description: The U.S. said it intercepted the drone strike, the first known attack on the Gulf country in two months.

item.title: Stellantis Offers to Repay C$24 Million to Canada but Government Says Automaker Breaching Commitments
item.description: Stellantis is offering to repay some of the money that Canada’s government wants to see returned for past support, but it won’t say if it’s prepared to defend in court the proposed sale of an Ontario plant.

item.title: Kim Jong Un Remakes North Korea’s Flag, Ditching Soviet-Era Version
item.description: The revamped flag marks a new effort by Kim to stamp his own identity on the country’s institutions.

item.title: Degrees Lead Nowhere. Jobs Don’t Exist. Welcome to India’s Youth Revolt.
item.description: Indian graduates are spending months cramming for long-shot civil-service exams, but their frustration is fueling anger toward Narendra Modi’s ruling party.

item.title: Putin Had Four Plans to Defeat Ukraine. He Only Has Two Left.
item.description: The Kremlin’s hopes for a military victory or a Trump-brokered deal have dimmed. Moscow is now betting on Ukraine’s economic collapse and weakening European support.

item.title: Iran’s New Cyber Playbook: Create Real-World Havoc
item.description: Tehran intensifies its effort to cause pain in the physical world with attacks on lightly protected tankers and refrigerators.

item.title: The U.S. Cut Cuba Off From the World’s Oil. Now It Runs on American Fuel.
item.description: Growing American fuel shipments are keeping Cuba afloat after Trump’s oil embargo pushed the island to the brink of a humanitarian crisis.

item.title: Oil Prices Rebound as Trump Questions Need for Iran Deal
item.description: Oil prices rebounded from initial losses and closed higher after President Trump said the U.S. doesn’t need a deal with Iran, putting some risk premium back into the market.

item.title: U.S. Army Officer Identified After U.K. Sting for Alleged Russian Spying
item.description: Lt. Col. Brandon Tyner was arrested after unwittingly speaking with British officials.

item.title: U.S. Collected $12 Billion in Venezuelan Oil Sales, Returning Nearly All of It
item.description: A State Department report shows Caracas has received most of the revenue, while Trump says the U.S. has profited from the oil sales.

item.title: A Mystery Businessman Introduced Jensen Huang to His Paramour. It Was Her Husband.
item.description: Kang Wei appeared to accept that his wife Alice Huang was in a romantic relationship and spoke openly of her closeness to the Nvidia chief.

item.title: Ukraine Says Its Military Starlink Is Disrupted Again, Hurting Defenses
item.description: Drones that rely on Starshield, a military version of SpaceX’s Starlink service, are losing connectivity if they fly faster than 100 miles an hour.

item.title: Israel Strikes Gaza Hospital, Killing at Least Six
item.description: The attack targeted Hamas militants, according to the Israeli military, and comes as progress on Trump’s Gaza Peace Plan is stalled.

item.title: Huang’s Coziness With Trump Wasn’t Enough to Save Him From Spying Scandal
item.description: U.S. officials have repeatedly raised concerns about his influence with the president and the Nvidia CEO’s posture toward China.

item.title: This Shipping Lane Is Now the World’s Deadliest. It Isn’t Hormuz.
item.description: Fatal attacks in the Black Sea have jumped, disrupting trade routes and posing a new test for NATO.

item.title: The ‘Peruvian Pope’ Returns Home to Elation
item.description: Chicago-born Pope Leo XIV spent two decades ministering in Peru, where citizens are welcoming him with a 45-foot statue, murals and T-shirts bearing his likeness.

item.title: The Spread of Cheaper Ballistic Missiles Rips Up Decades of Military Thinking
item.description: As interceptor supplies run down, Iran and the Houthis have shown how American bases are increasingly vulnerable.

item.title: Bessent Moved to Military Base After Threats Linked to Iran
item.description: The Treasury secretary has led the administration’s economic pressure campaign against Tehran.

item.title: JD Vance Emerges as Lead Iran Negotiator
item.description: Plus, Democrats are pointing fingers after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth avoided impeachment, and United Airlines will ban AI bots from booking its flights.
